action_trace.summary: Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals around multi-valued field aggregation semantics, unbounded SORT+MV_EXPAND error clarity, and acceptance criteria for improved error messaging in ES|QL. Questions target end-user mental models, pain points, and validation of proposed solutions.

Interview questions designed to elicit user goals (workflow impact, success criteria), pain points (current error confusion, multi-value aggregation handling), and acceptance criteria (error message clarity, command-specific guidance) using 5W1H and Socratic techniques grounded in ES|QL SORT/MV_EXPAND and multi-value aggregation requirements.

Chain-of-Thought decomposition: (1) Multi-valued field aggregation semantics require clarification on null-handling expectations and user mental models; (2) SORT+MV_EXPAND error messaging is a critical pain point requiring explicit command naming and remediation guidance; (3) Acceptance criteria span error clarity, documentation, and query validation. Interview targets user goals (aggregation predictability), pain points (error opacity, unbounded sort limitations), and acceptance criteria (error message specificity, preventive validation). Techniques applied: 5W1H framing, Socratic iteration, life-cycle trade-off exploration (error clarity vs. feature scope).

End users need clearer ES|QL error messaging for SORT+MV_EXPAND conflicts and predictable multi-value field aggregation semantics to reduce query debugging overhead and improve statistical accuracy in business analytics workflows.

End users require explicit error messaging for SORT+MV_EXPAND conflicts and predictable, documented multi-value field aggregation semantics to enable reliable business reporting and self-service query debugging without manual intervention.

End users require explicit, command-specific error messages for SORT+MV_EXPAND failures and clearly documented, predictable null-handling semantics for multi-value field aggregations to enable reliable financial reporting and efficient query debugging.

Five clarification questions targeting ambiguous multi-value field aggregation semantics (null handling, expression evaluation, result composition), SORT+MV_EXPAND error messaging specificity, and whether these behaviors are design constraints or temporary limitations requiring explicit user handling.

Three clarification questions on multi-value field semantics (uniform vs. value-specific null handling, aggregation counting vs. summing), error message prescription level, plus one conflict (incomplete requirement example) and one scope ambiguity (expression context applicability).

Six clarification questions raised to resolve ambiguities in multi-value field semantics (null handling, aggregation behavior), SUM aggregation interpretation (cardinality-based vs. arithmetic), and error message design (diagnosis vs. prescription) for ES|QL requirements, grounded in pain points around statistical correctness and error message actionability.

End-user confirmed multi-value field aggregation semantics: arithmetic sum for base field (18 = 3+5+10), null exclusion for expressions on multi-values (7 = only single-value contribution). Refined error messaging to combine diagnosis with actionable fix prescription. Identified need for explicit documentation of null handling rules and value-level vs. document-level application semantics.

End-user requirements validated and refined: (1) multi-value field null handling confirmed as document-level for expressions like X+a, (2) aggregation arithmetic semantics clarified for mixed single/multi-valued documents, (3) error message scope refined to include both diagnosis and prescriptive fix for SORT+MV_EXPAND unbounded errors, (4) documentation requirement added to prevent statistical confusion in business reporting workflows.

End-user confirms multi-value field null handling semantics (expressions like X+a evaluate null for multi-valued documents), validates aggregation consistency (arithmetic sum across mixed documents), and refines error message requirement to provide both diagnosis and actionable fix ('Add LIMIT after MV_EXPAND before SORT'). Requirements are now clear, predictable, and documented for business reporting reliability.

Consolidated 7 structured elicitation records from EndUser dialogue addressing two critical ES|QL requirements: (1) multi-value field null handling semantics in aggregations with confirmed behavior that expressions on multi-valued fields evaluate to null for entire document contribution, and (2) enhanced error messaging for unbounded SORT + MV_EXPAND queries requiring both diagnostic clarity and actionable remediation guidance. Records align with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 traceability, include MoSCoW prioritization, and specify validation/documentation needs for Q1 2026 delivery.

Eight targeted deployment-focused questions probing infrastructure scaling limits for MV_EXPAND, performance boundaries, error observability, security/governance implications, validation layer placement, backward compatibility risks, operational runbooks, and pre-deployment testing requirements for the ES|QL multi-value field null-handling and error-message improvements.

Seven targeted questions probe deployer constraints across infrastructure capacity (cluster topology, unbounded sort resource limits), security (query exposure, access control), scalability (query volume, auto-suggestion capability), error message integration (delivery channels, backward compatibility), indexing strategy (multi-valued field storage), and operational readiness (documentation, training requirements). Chain-of-Thought reasoning: (1) identified three core requirement clusters (null semantics, aggregation correctness, error messaging), (2) mapped each to deployer concerns (operational, security, technical), (3) formulated questions balancing diagnostic depth with actionable constraint discovery per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 stakeholder analysis.

Targeted Deployer dialogue probing infrastructure capacity for MV_EXPAND row expansion, security constraints on error message visibility and audit logging of null-handling semantics, scalability strategy for distributed aggregations on multi-valued financial datasets, and operational procedures for communicating enhanced error messages and LIMIT requirements to end-users.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness for ES|QL multi-value field semantics (null handling for X+a expressions) and enhanced SORT+MV_EXPAND error messaging. Key constraints: sub-100ms error generation latency, O(1) pattern detection scalability, sanitized error outputs for security, and pre-execution validation checkpoints. Operational procedures mandate diagnostic logging and fail-fast rejection with actionable remediation guidance. Cost optimization via parse-time LIMIT enforcement prevents unbounded expansion.

Deployer response establishes infrastructure constraints (sub-100ms validation latency, <5MB cache per node), security mandates (sanitized error messages, no schema leakage, multi-tenant isolation), scalability targets (linear validation complexity, distributed caching), and operational procedures (diagnostic logging, performance monitoring, documentation) to support enhanced SORT+MV_EXPAND error messages without degrading cluster performance or exposing sensitive metadata.

Deployer confirms infrastructure support for enhanced SORT+MV_EXPAND error messaging within existing ES|QL stack with <100ms latency, <5MB per-node overhead, and zero new microservices. Security mandates sanitization of command names and AST structures. Scalability targets support >1000-operation queries with early-exit detection at parsing phase. Operational procedures include feature flag rollout strategy and latency monitoring. Cost-optimized through parser reuse rather than external validation systems.

Deployer raises six critical clarifications: (1) error message sanitization scope and schema metadata exposure boundaries; (2) latency-completeness trade-off for prescriptive error guidance; (3) expression null-handling scope across arithmetic and comparison operators; (4) error context caching architecture and eviction policy; (5) balance between diagnostic and prescriptive error messaging; (6) null contribution rules for aggregation functions beyond SUM. These clarifications resolve operational context gaps for secure, performant implementation of enhanced SORT+MV_EXPAND error messages and multi-value field null semantics within infrastructure constraints.

Deployer raises five critical clarifications on error message sanitization scope, latency-completeness trade-offs, multi-value null handling expression coverage, error generation architecture within parsing stack, and SORT+MV_EXPAND detection timing to resolve ambiguities between security mandates, infrastructure constraints, and refined user requirements before implementation.

Deployer raises six critical clarifications on error message sanitization boundaries, latency-completeness trade-offs, null-handling expression scope, cache constraints, validation timing, and financial use-case semantics. All require stakeholder confirmation before implementation to ensure security compliance, performance targets, and semantic correctness for multi-value field aggregations.

Deployer validates and refines elasticsearch_2026q1 requirements: (1) Multi-value null handling semantics confirmed as uniform application to all expressions on multi-valued fields; (2) Enhanced error message requirement operationalized with sanitization constraints, <100ms latency, and actionable fix prescription; (3) Infrastructure constraints satisfied via existing query parsing stack with <5MB caching overhead; (4) Security mandate enforced through command name sanitization and AST structure masking; (5) Deployment-ready validation rules for SORT+MV_EXPAND pattern detection. All deployer clarifications resolved; system ready for implementation sprint.

Deployer confirms all three core requirements (multi-value null handling, enhanced error messages, unbounded SORT detection) are deployable within infrastructure constraints (<100ms latency, <5MB memory, existing stack). Security sanitization scope clarified. Expression scope encompasses all arithmetic/logical operators on multi-valued fields. Recommend phased 3-sprint rollout with latency validation baseline.

Deployer validation confirms three core requirements are deployable within infrastructure, security, and latency constraints: (1) multi-value null handling semantics via aggregation engine modification (<1% CPU cost); (2) enhanced error messages with diagnosis + prescription in <100ms via query parsing layer integration (<5MB memory); (3) security sanitization via token masking without external services. All deployer clarifications resolved. Ready for implementation phase.

Operating environment specification for Elasticsearch 2026Q1 ES|QL multi-value field semantics: cluster nodes require 5MB error caching capacity and <100ms query validation latency; security mandate prohibits AST/schema exposure in sanitized error messages; error generation pipeline integrates within existing parser without external microservices; multi-value field expressions evaluate to null uniformly for document contributions; SORT+MV_EXPAND validation detects unbounded patterns and prescribes LIMIT placement within latency budget.

Seven system requirements consolidated from user, environment, and deployer perspectives addressing multi-value field null semantics in aggregations (SYS-REQ-ES2026Q1-001), enhanced error messaging for SORT+MV_EXPAND patterns (SYS-REQ-ES2026Q1-002), security sanitization (SYS-REQ-ES2026Q1-003), architectural integration (SYS-REQ-ES2026Q1-004), performance constraints (SYS-REQ-ES2026Q1-005), expression scope clarification (SYS-REQ-ES2026Q1-006), and supporting documentation (SYS-REQ-ES2026Q1-007). All requirements validated against IEEE 830 format with traceability to interview records, user confirmations, deployer validations, and infrastructure constraints. Requirements balance diagnostic completeness with <100ms latency, <5MB memory overhead, and zero operational complexity additions.

Selected SysML (Block Definition + Internal Block Diagram) as primary modeling methodology with UML Sequence Diagram for error flow analysis. SysML provides hierarchical functional decomposition and constraint mapping essential for coordinating three requirement clusters (multi-value null semantics, enhanced error messaging, infrastructure constraints) across heterogeneous stakeholders. Identified consistency: null-handling semantics uniformly apply to all expressions on multi-valued fields; latency-completeness trade-off is achievable via pre-computed diagnosis templates. Recommended diagram structure includes BDD (functional blocks), IBD (data/control flow), parametric constraints (latency/memory), and traceability matrix to SYS-REQ-* allocations.

Constructed SysML/PlantUML requirement model for elasticsearch_2026q1 highlighting three critical gaps: (1) unresolved conflict between <100ms latency constraint and requirement for comprehensive diagnosis+actionable-fix error messages, (2) semantic inconsistency regarding multi-valued document contributions to SUM(X) vs. SUM(X+a) aggregations, (3) incomplete traceability from system requirements back to user requirements and unresolved clarification questions on expression scope, sanitization scope, and error message format specificity. Model identifies decomposition opportunity for SYS-REQ-ES2026Q1-002 (SORT+MV_EXPAND detection) and missing documentation requirement definition. Recommend resolving latency-completeness trade-off and clarifying multi-value null-handling scope before implementation sprint.
